claims.text: The measured excess on this trip clears both gates in POL-RD-01. The GPS trace records 27.18 km driven against a booked optimal of 21.0 km, an excess of 6.18 km — greater than the 0.8 km absolute gate and 29.43% of the optimal, greater than the 20% gate. Both establishment tests pass, so the route deviation is ESTABLISHED.

The governing distance is the trace, not the rounded trip-record copy. POL-RD-01 provides that where gps_trace.trace_distance_km and trip_record.actual_distance_km disagree, the trace governs and the trip-record figure may not be cited for the threshold test. Here trace_distance_km is 27.18 km and trip_record.actual_distance_km is 27.2 km, and the excess computed from the trace-derived figure still clears both gates, so nothing turns on the rounding.

The trace is clean and needs no corroboration. Under POL-RD-07 the trace is impaired for policy purposes only if it contains a gap over 90 seconds, a straight-line jump over 500 m, or a sustained sampling interval above 30 seconds; this trace shows point_count 229, gaps [], max_gap_sec 0.0 and sample_interval_sec 10s, so none of limbs (a) to (c) fires and the excess stands proven on the trace alone.

No traffic advisory exonerates the detour, and the absence is itself citable. The only advisory artifact in the bundle, EV-ADVIS-00101-01, carries no payload: no road or junction is named, no validity window, no alternative-route length. POL-RD-03 requires all three before any excess is exonerated, so the clause cannot be run and no part of the 6.18 km excess is excused.

POL-RD-04 does not apply. The chat log's only rider message (at 10:41:12) asks why the car is heading toward the city centre — it objects to the route, it does not request a waypoint — and every message on the trip carries waypoint_hint null, so the field comparison the clause requires is undecidable and no distance is excluded as rider-requested.

POL-RD-05 relocation does not apply. pickup_amended_at and dropoff_amended_at are both null and amended_optimal_distance_km is null, so there is no amended endpoint and the booked optimal of 21.0 km is the correct baseline.

This is not a pooled trip, so POL-RD-12 cannot reduce the baseline. vehicle_type is RYDE_X and solo_optimal_distance_km is null; there is no matched pooled itinerary on the record, and the 21.0 km optimal on the trip record is the figure the threshold is measured against.

The rider has discharged her burden under POL-RD-08 and the burden has shifted to the driver. The trip identifier TRP-00101 matches across trip_record, gps_trace and fare_breakdown, the pickup timestamp 10:21:05 matches, and the trace shows a threshold-crossing excess. The driver must now point to a specific artifact and clause to excuse it, and he points to none: his own chat message MSG-00101-002 ('sorry boss missed the exit, coming back now') concedes a navigation error, which no clause excuses.

The fare model is METERED, so POL-RD-02 governs and the refund is arithmetic. On the constants and the 1.0 surge read from fare_breakdown.surge_multiplier: recomputed_fare = (3.80 + 0.75x21.0 + 0.28x26.0) x 1.0 + 0.80 platform fee = 27.63; refund = 35.64 charged_total - 27.63 = 8.01, rounded up to 8.05 payable. There are no ERP or toll lines to add and no promo discount.

The refund is neither de minimis nor large enough to be a full refund. At 8.01 it is far above the SGD 0.50 de minimis floor, so money must move; and at 22.47% of charged_total it does not reach the 90% full_refund_share, so the correct ruling value is PARTIAL_REFUND of 8.05, not the $10.00 the rider estimated by hand.

No separate pass-through correction under POL-RD-09 arises on this trip: the fare breakdown's erp_gantries array is empty and tolls_erp is 0.0, so the whole remedy is the POL-RD-02 distance-and-time refund and no gantry or surcharge line can be double-counted on top of it.

The rider filed this dispute, so the party-relative reading of NO_ACTION under POL-GEN-03 matters: a NO_ACTION outcome would leave the overcharged $35.64 exactly as charged. Because the record establishes a refundable excess, the ruling must be PARTIAL_REFUND and the present charge cannot stand.

That excess is real, but it is NOT a MATERIAL deviation: it falls below BOTH of POL-RD-01's materiality thresholds (greater than 50% of optimal_distance_km, and greater than 8.0 km absolute). The consequence is that the POL-RD-06 driver_profile check is not engaged, no driver-conduct referral follows, and no FULL_REFUND uplift of charged_total is available. The remedy is confined to the POL-RD-02 partial refund.

Independently of materiality, the driver's trailing-90-day record is clean and cannot support a pattern finding: driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 0 against completed_trips_90d of 812 — a ratio of 0.00, far below the 0.05 ratio threshold POL-RD-06 sets and far below its alternative 3-flag trigger. No repeat-deviation pattern is established on these figures, so none of the POL-RD-06(a), (b) or (c) effects can fire against this driver.

ruling.explanation:
To the rider and to the driver — this is a route-deviation case on trip TRP-00101, and both advocates actually converge on the same figures, which I accept.

Is the deviation established? Yes. The platform's GPS trace (EV-GPS-00101) records 27.18 km against the booked optimal of 21.0 km on the trip record (EV-TRIP-00101) — an excess of 6.18 km, or 29.4%. Both of POL-RD-01's establishment gates pass (excess above 20% of optimal, and above 0.8 km absolute). The trace figure governs over the rounded trip-record copy of 27.2 km, as POL-RD-01 requires; nothing turns on the 0.02 km rounding. The trace is clean for POL-RD-07 purposes — 229 fixes, no gaps, max_gap 0.0 s, 10-second sampling — so no independent corroboration is needed to prove the excess, and the driver's own chat message MSG-00101-002 ('sorry boss missed the exit, coming back now') and his submitted statement confirm the navigation error anyway.

Does anything excuse it? No. There is no traffic advisory in the bundle (EV-ADVIS-00101-01 is empty), so POL-RD-03 cannot run. The rider requested no waypoint — every waypoint_hint is null and her message only objects to the route — so POL-RD-04 is unavailable. No endpoint was amended (POL-RD-05) and this is not a pooled trip (vehicle_type RYDE_X, solo_optimal null), so POL-RD-12 does not apply.

How much? The fare model is METERED, so POL-RD-02 governs and the number is arithmetic, not discretionary. Reading the surge multiplier from fare_breakdown.surge_multiplier (1.0): recomputed fare = (3.80 base + 0.75 x 21.0 km + 0.28 x 26.0 min) x 1.0 + 0.80 platform fee = 27.63. Refund = 35.64 charged_total - 27.63 = 8.01, rounded UP to the nearest SGD 0.05 = 8.05. That is above the SGD 0.50 de-minimis floor but only 22.5% of charged_total, well under the 90% full-refund share, so the ruling is PARTIAL_REFUND of 8.05, not the $10.00 the rider estimated by hand. There is no ERP, toll or surcharge line to add on top (erp_gantries empty, tolls 0.00, no airport surcharge), so POL-RD-09 makes no separate correction and nothing is double-counted. Driver compensation does not arise: the rider was billed 27.2 km against a 27.18 km trace, so there is no unbilled-distance shortfall under POL-RD-04.

The materiality point both advocates raise is accepted: at 29.4% and 6.18 km this excess falls below BOTH of POL-RD-01's materiality thresholds (50% and 8.0 km), so it is not a MATERIAL deviation, the POL-RD-06 driver-profile check is not triggered, and no driver-conduct referral follows. Independently, the driver's trailing-90-day record shows 0 deviation flags across 812 completed trips (ratio 0.00), so no repeat pattern could be established even if the check had been required. No clause in the policy produces a referral on these facts, so the referrals list is empty.

Amount moved: 8.05 SGD to the rider. The present charge of 35.64 does not stand in full; 27.63 of it does.

No excuse applies. The driver himself conceded a navigation error in chat (MSG-00101-002, 10:42) and in his counterparty statement. To the driver: the concession and the 6.18 km excess make the refund owed, but it is confined to the distance-and-time difference.

The fare model is METERED, so POL-RD-02 governs and the refund is arithmetic. No separate pass-through correction under POL-RD-09 arises on this trip: the fare breakdown's erp_gantries array is empty and tolls_erp is 0.0, so the whole remedy is the POL-RD-02 distance-and-time refund and no gantry or surcharge line can be double-counted on top of it.

The rider filed this dispute, so the party-relative reading of NO_ACTION under POL-GEN-03 matters: a NO_ACTION outcome would leave the overcharged $35.64 exactly as charged. Because the record establishes a refundable excess, the ruling must be PARTIAL_REFUND and the present charge cannot stand.

The platform's own GPS trace measures 27.18 km against a booked optimal of 21.0 km — an excess of 6.18 km, or 29.4% of optimal. The consequence is that the POL-RD-06 driver_profile check is not engaged, no driver-conduct referral follows, and no FULL_REFUND uplift of charged_total is available. The quantum is capped by the POL-RD-02 arithmetic, which the fare_breakdown has already computed: recomputed_fare = (3.80 base + 0.75 x 21.0 km + 0.28 x 26.0 min) x 1.0 (the surge_multiplier read from the FARE_BREAKDOWN, not the trip_record) + 0.80 platform fee + 0 ERP/surcharge/waiting - 0 promo = 27.63; refund = 35.64 charged_total - 27.63 = 8.01, rounded UP to the nearest SGD 0.05 = 8.05.
